What to know

  • Glycogen is made and broken down by separate pathways. Glycogenesis uses glycogen synthase and branching enzyme; glycogenolysis uses glycogen phosphorylase and debranching enzyme.
  • Glycolysis has two phases. The investment phase consumes 2 ATP; the payoff phase produces 4 ATP and 2 NADH, for a net gain of 2 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose.
  • Pyruvate has two fates. Aerobic cells convert it to acetyl-CoA; anaerobic cells reduce it to lactate to regenerate NAD⁺.
  • Phosphofructokinase-1 is the committed step. ATP and citrate inhibit it; AMP, ADP, and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate activate it.
  • Insulin and glucagon set the direction. Insulin favors glycogen synthesis and glycolysis; glucagon favors glycogen breakdown and gluconeogenesis in the liver.

Check

check.question: What is the net ATP yield of glycolysis per glucose?
check.explanation: Two ATP are invested and four are produced, so the net gain is two ATP, plus two NADH.
